summary: The v0.5.16 crash came from canonical prefill-CP arguments being projected into two mutually exclusive legacy enable fields. Those legacy fields and projections are absent at the prepared base. Added an issue-specific regression proving the canonical DeepSeek V4 interleave path reaches the current validator and CP handler without recreating the conflict, plus invalid-strategy and disabled-CP boundaries.

tests.what_was_measured: Three current-source argument-resolution tests: the reported unified interleave CLI path, rejection of DeepSeek V4 zigzag, and disabled-CP default preservation; 3 passed.
Repository formatting, lint, AST, spelling, and registered-test metadata checks for the changed test file.

Broader class run: the 3 new tests and 2 other tests passed, while 2 pre-existing CUDA-assuming tests failed on the prepared HIP host at the intentional HIP prefill-CP deprecation guard. This is retained as environment evidence, not counted as issue-specific failure.

gpu_execution.evidence: The issue is an argument-validation failure before GPU execution. The assigned device was inventoried as one AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) with ROCm 7.2; current source intentionally rejects prefill CP on HIP. No GPU kernel was run or used to qualify the 8x NVIDIA H20 workload. See reports/j-9e90d43ddd63/raw/gpu-inventory.txt.

remaining_limitations: The reported eight NVIDIA H20 GPUs and CUDA 12.9 environment were unavailable; only one AMD gfx950 GPU was assigned.
Current source intentionally rejects prefill CP on HIP, so model startup and distributed engine execution could not be tested on the assigned GPU.
The regression validates the exact CLI and argument-hook conflict, not DeepSeek V4 model semantics, CUDA kernels, eight-rank collectives, or performance.
